title: Embed cursor idempotency, backoff hints, and pagination error mapping spec
creator: Aisha Morgan
description:
Goal: Define a forward-compatible compatibility layer that standardizes cursor semantics across legacy embed/rerank clients, provides clear idempotency guarantees for paginated iterators, and surfaces machine-readable backoff/retry hints so SDKs and clients can converge on predictable behavior without requiring immediate client changes.

Background: Multiple customers and SDKs expect different semantics from our embeddings/rerank pagination endpoints: some expect strict cursor-idempotency (replaying a cursor yields the same page), others accept best-effort eventual consistency and rely on Retry-After headers. Differences have caused customer-facing flakiness when we roll runtime changes and during cross-region failover. Existing tickets have focused on error-code normalization and cursor stability, but lack a concise compatibility playbook for adapter behavior and SDK contracts.

This ticket produces the spec that eng will implement in the compatibility adapter/proxy and that SDKs will reference for graceful migration. Key outcomes: canonical mapping of HTTP errors -> client action (retry / backoff / abort), header-based backoff hints (Retry-After, X-Redwood-Backoff-Hint), explicit idempotency metadata in paginated responses (cursor_tombstone, stable_until), and a deprecation/migration timeline for legacy cursor behaviors.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility adapter implements HTTP -> action mapping doc and returns Retry-After or X-Redwood-Backoff-Hint when appropriate
Paginated responses include optional idempotency metadata fields (cursor_tombstone, stable_until) in a backwards-compatible way (fields omitted for legacy clients)
Adapter guarantees that replays of cursors marked as 'idempotent' return identical results for stable_until window; outside window returns tombstone with guidance header
SDK teams have reviewed and agreed on retry/backoff semantics and will ship minor SDK updates to honor headers
E2E canary run in staging shows <0.5% client-observed pagination inconsistencies for 48h under mixed legacy+updated clients
Monitoring dashboards created: rate of tombstone responses, Retry-After usage, client-side retry spike, and customer errors per region
Documentation and migration guide published to Confluence and linked in breaking-changes email to top customers
tasks: Finalize HTTP code -> client action matrix (PM + runtime leads)
Design header schema for backoff hints and idempotency metadata (Design: create examples and SDK snippets)
Implement adapter transform rules in compatibility proxy (ENG) and add feature flag for rollout
Add telemetry hooks to surface tombstone, retry-after, and cursor mismatch events
Update JS + Python SDKs to read X-Redwood-Backoff-Hint and prefer header-driven retries
Create canary plan: 10% traffic to adapter, observe 48h, then expand
Author migration guide and sample code for handling tombstones and idempotent cursor replays
notes: 2026-02-22 - Kickoff: scoped to HTTP mapping + header-driven hints. Eng to prototype X-Redwood-Backoff-Hint format (ms jitter window + exponential metadata).
2026-02-27 - Design review: prefer header over body for backoff so legacy clients can ignore safely. Agreed to keep new fields optional and additive.

2026-03-03 - Engineering update: prototype adapter returns 'X-Redwood-Backoff-Hint: 1500;mode=exponential;max=10000' and 'X-Redwood-Idempotency: stable_until=2026-03-10T12:00Z;cursor_id=abc123'. Need to formalize grammar.
2026-03-05 - PM note: include tombstone response body pattern for cases where cursor is expired and cannot be replayed. This will contain 'tombstone_reason' and 'next_cursor_suggestion'.
2026-03-07 - SDK sync: JS team accepts header parsing; Python team requests example of best-effort fallback when headers missing (suggestion: exponential-backoff with capped retries).
2026-03-10 - Ready for review: spec uploaded to Confluence. Seeking sign-off from Runtime, SDK, and Security leads. Canary plan attached in links.
review_feedback: Runtime lead (Diego Ramirez): ensure adapter preserves streaming semantics for streaming embedding endpoints; do not buffer entire result to synthesize headers
SDK lead (Meera Patel): prefer explicit API that returns 'cursorStatus' object rather than parsing header strings in long-term SDK design
Security (Hannah Lee): header syntax acceptable; ensure no PII is emitted in cursor metadata and add KMS review if we sign tokens
Customer Success (Oliver Grant): ask to prioritize a short migration checklist for top 10 customers using legacy cursors
communication_plan: Post an RFC to #runtime-api with the finalized mapping and header spec
Publish migration guide on Confluence and include SDK snippets
Email top-20 customers with expected behavioral changes and offer migration calls
Run two-stage canary: staging -> 5% prod -> 25% prod -> global, with rollback gates
